(p-176) **The Sura of Al-Qadr (The Night of Decree): its purpose**

It details the matter that is one of the two parts of what the purpose of "Read" (Iqra', sura 96) contained. Its name indicates this, because the night was given its excellence by it. This is an instance of naming the effect by its cause (*ithlaq al-musabbab 'ala al-sabab*). It is also evidence for those who hold that times are honored on account of what happens in them, as that Jew said on the day when God the Exalted revealed ﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you﴾ (al-Ma'idah 5:3). Al-Faruq 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, singled out that day for this and informed him that for us it had become two festivals: a festival because it was the Day of 'Arafah, and a festival because it was a Friday.

﴿In the name of God﴾, whose command is majestic and whose essence is exalted. ﴿The Most Merciful﴾, whose mercy is all-encompassing, so that His attributes flourish. ﴿The Most Compassionate﴾, who specially granted the People of Tawhid the completion of blessing, so that His gardens were reserved for them.

* *

When God the Exalted, glorified be He, mentioned His Book in this Arabic Qur'an, which is inimitable, He mentioned its sending down while it is kept present in every heart. This made it unnecessary to repeat it by explicit name. So whenever He referred to it by pronoun, the addressee knew it from the indicators in the context and from the greatness it holds in the heart and the presence it has in the mind. This is especially so in this sura, since it opened with the command to recite (the Qur'an) at the start of al-'Alaq, and it ended with prayer, which is the greatest of its pillars. Thus its indication of it was extremely clear, as if He had said: "and draw near by reciting the Qur'an in prayer." So its concealment (by pronoun) was more indicative of overwhelming greatness than its disclosure would have been, because the pronoun indicates that nothing is complete that sends down anything other than it, so it is of such standing that it need not be explicitly named. He magnified it by several matters: its pronominal concealment; the attribution of its sending down to Himself; placing this in the locus of greatness; and magnifying the time of its sending down, which includes the greatness of the land in which it was sent down, according to the opinion of most scholars, and the Prophet to whom it was sent down. He emphasized it (with *inna*), because of the denial that they held,

﴿Indeed We﴾, that is, by virtue of Our greatness, ﴿sent it down﴾, that is, this whole Reminder from the Preserved Tablet to the House of Majesty in the lowest heaven, arranged in this order by which God gathered the protected community, and which exists now. Likewise was the sending down of its first portion, and that is the beginning of the preceding sura (al-'Alaq), a sending down that confirms that its greatness derives from Our greatness, by virtue of its inimitability in its composition, and because strengths fall short of comprehending its knowledge. The first part of it sent down was its opening, up to five verses of it, [the last of which is] ﴿what he did not know﴾ (al-'Alaq 96:5), upon the Prophet ﷺ, while he was secluding himself during this blessed month at Mount Hira', one of the mountains of blessed Makkah. Then it began to descend in portions according to events, until it was completed over twenty-three years. Whenever a portion of it descended, the Prophet ﷺ was commanded concerning its arrangement within its sura, by the command of God the Exalted, until the suras were completed in the form they now have, which is the form they have in the House of Majesty.

When He had magnified it by what He mentioned, He increased its greatness by the time He chose for its sending down, so that its beginning would be blessed, since its effect is praiseworthy. So He said: ﴿in the Night of Decree﴾, that is, the night which has great worth and great nobility, and the deeds performed in it have worth and nobility. Thus it was as though it were specifically characterized by *qadr* (decree/worth), so no other night has any *qadr*.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: He returned to a declaration about the sending down of what had been commanded to be read, because the indication had already preceded concerning the great matter of the Books, and that the path to Him, glorified be He, is only through that gate. God the Exalted informed us of the night of its sending down and made us aware of its worth, so that we would rely upon it in the places where we seek His answer, attach our hopes to it, and strive diligently in deeds, perhaps we would coincide with it. It is like the hour on Friday in the obscurity of its matter together with the sublime nature of its worth, and of the same kind as the Middle Prayer. For God, glorified be He, there is the greatest mercy in concealing this. In making known the great worth of this night was also making known the sublimity of the descent within it. Thus the Sura of al-Qadr became a completion of what preceded it, and its connection became clear. End of quotation.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 97, verse 2:

When he (al-Biqa'i) knew from the context that it (the Night of Power) is magnified by the greatness of what was sent down in it, and by the expression used for it with this (phrase), he said, emphasizing that magnification, as an exhortation to striving in its revival (ihya'), because (p-179) a person has, from laziness and the tendency toward idleness (batalah), what discourages him from that: ﴿And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is?﴾ That is: and what has made you know, while you are most diligent in inquiry? ﴿What is the Night of Decree?﴾ That is: your comprehension does not reach it, even though you are the most knowledgeable of people regarding the utmost of its excellence and the ultimate of its rank, with your breadth of knowledge, the comprehensiveness of your thought, and your great endowments.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 97, verse 3:

Since its greatness has been established by drawing attention to the fact that it is worthy of being asked about its distinguishing features, He says, beginning a new sentence: ﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾. That is, the night which We singled out by Our sending down [the Qur'an] in it. ﴿Better than a thousand months﴾, meaning: free of it [the Night of Decree], or the deed performed in it is better than the deed performed in a thousand months in which there is no Night of Decree. That is eighty-three years and four months. They said: this is equal to the duration of the rule of the Banu Umayyah. Its being named thus is due to its nobility and the greatness of its status, or because the affairs and decrees are distinguished in it from the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab), so that the ruling about what will happen from that night until its like in the coming year is written in it by God, from the saying of them: "God decreed (qaddara) this matter, decreeing it a decree (qadran)," that is, He decided it. It is the night intended in Surah al-Dukhan by His words, Exalted is He: ﴿In it every wise matter is distinguished﴾ [al-Dukhan: 4]. The mention of the thousand is either for emphasis, by reaching the utmost limit of numerical magnitudes, so that it is more eloquent than seventy in magnifying it; or because the Prophet ﷺ mentioned a man from among the believers of the Children of Israel who wore weapons fighting in the way of God for a thousand months, so the believers marvelled at him, and their deeds seemed meagre to them; so God, glorified and exalted is He, gave them a night whoever stands in worship during it (p-180) would be better than that. He concealed it in the last ten nights of the month of Ramadan according to the majority opinion, based on what is authentically established from the hadiths, so that they would strive to attain it, just as He concealed the hour of answered supplication on the day of Friday, the middle prayer among the five, His Greatest Name among the names, His pleasure in all acts of obedience so that they would be eager for all of them, His displeasure in acts of disobedience so that they would refrain from all of them, and the Hour of Resurrection among the times, so that they would strive in every moment out of caution against its arrival. The secret in this is that what is precious is not reached except through great striving, to show its preciousness, to magnify the desire for it, and to announce joy in it. However, the surah being thirty words equal, which favours that they are the twenty-seventh word, which corresponds to His saying "it" (hiya), as transmitted from Abu Bakr al-Warraq.

Since he had magnified it, he mentioned the aspect of its greatness, so that it would be an announcement after ambiguity, which is more striking to the soul. So he said, beginning a new sentence: ﴿The angels descend﴾, meaning a descent that proceeds gradually, which in its origin is of the utmost lightness and swiftness, indicated by the omission of the ta' (of the verb's feminine marker) (...). ﴿and the Spirit﴾, meaning Jibril, upon him be peace. He is singled out to explain his excellence, or he is together with the noblest of the angels, or he is a creature greater than the angels, or he is a matter in which the hearts of the knowers find tranquility and through which blessing and goodness are obtained. ﴿therein﴾. He indicated the obscurity of that descent by dropping the ta' of "tanazzul" [with] what preceded of allusions, and he showed the increase of blessing in that descent and the great obedience of the angels by His saying: ﴿by the permission of their Lord﴾, meaning by the knowledge of the One who does good to them, who nurtures them and empowers them, and [who] sends them down to the earth or to the lowest heaven, or brings them near to the believers, the descent being initiated [by Him]. ﴿concerning every matter﴾, meaning the universal affairs about which they, by the permission of [Allah], distribute the details of the matters that He, glory be to Him, wills in that year at their appointed times, from that night until its like in the coming year; or for the sake of the decree of everything that will occur in that year. He expressed "thing" by "matter" to inform that they do nothing except by His command.

When Allah, glorified is He, mentioned these virtues, the outcome was that the night is characterized by complete safety, just as Paradise, which is its cause, is characterized by it. This is more indicative of its greatness, so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Peace it is﴾, meaning it is very great. ﴿It is﴾, meaning it is nothing but safety and goodness, with no evil in it, and that peace and blessing continue in it ﴿until﴾, meaning up to ﴿the emergence of dawn﴾, meaning its rising, the time of its rising, and the place of its rising. In it there is no evil, unlike other nights. So the sun does not rise on its morning between the two horns of Satan, God willing, and this is the secret of al-Kisa'i's reading [with a kasra (ﻛﺴﺮﺓ)], and Allah knows best. The expression "ḥattā" (until) was chosen instead of "ilā" (to) so that it would be understood that what follows it takes the ruling of what precedes it, so the dawn takes the ruling of the night.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that Jibril, peace be upon him, descends on the Night of Power (laylat al-qadr) in a host of angels, and with him is a green banner, which he plants upon the Ka'bah. Then he disperses the angels among the people, so that they greet every standing, sitting, remembering, bowing, and prostrating person, until the dawn rises. Whoever contemplates this surah will know from it the greatness of the Qur'an, and will turn to it wholeheartedly, reciting it with its due recitation, as commanded in the surah "Read" (iqra'). Thus he will be safe, without doubt, from the terror of the Day of Judgment mentioned in "al-Tin." From reciting it with its due right comes the glorification of the Night of Power because of what has been mentioned of its nobility. This leads to eagerness to seek it throughout the year; if that is not possible, then in every Ramadan; if that is not possible, then in all the nights of the last ten days of it, so that he may have from the deeds, because of its virtue and the multiplication of reward for deeds performed in it, what no one can count before Allah, to the extent that it may be better than the deeds of one who strove for a thousand years before us.

The return of its end to its beginning, by the fact that this descent in the Night of Power is upon its first part, is most clear, because the greatest peace in it is the descent of the Qur'an. Perhaps the fact that it is thirty words (in the surah) is an indication that the caliphate of prophethood, which lasted thirty years after the death of the Prophet (ﷺ), whose last part was on the day when the Commander of the Faithful al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, relinquished the caliphate to Mu'awiyah, may Allah be pleased with him, in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal in the year forty-one, is like the Night of Power in time, and what follows it is like the nights of the year, in which the virtuous and others (dwell). That period belonged to five caliphs, indicated by the letters of the last word in it. The alif is for Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and it is most appropriate for him, for the Rabbaniyyun (the masters of spiritual knowledge) said: it is the name of the Standing, the All-Encompassing, the Supreme, who is absent from His station, yet He is present with it in existence like the spirit. Likewise was he, may Allah be pleased with him, present with the Ummah by his existence while being absent from them by his turning, and all his heart was only with Allah, mighty and majestic. The lam is for 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, and it is most appropriate for him, for it is a connection between the inner part of the alif and the outer part of the mim, which belongs to Muhammad (ﷺ), because it is for completion. He did likewise: he joined the two conduct (sirah) with a complete joining, such that the weakness of al-Siddiq in his body was joined with the strength of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the matter of Allah, until the affair was ordered by him with an order beyond which there is no increase. The fa' is for 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, and it indicates the beginning of the pure essence of his nature to a transition with increase or decrease. Its sign is the primordial nature (al-fitrah al-ula), and its sensible sign is milk at the first moment of its emergence, for when the slightest amount of extended air touches it, it changes it. Likewise, the natural disposition, when the slightest amount of desire aimed at it touches it, changes it. Thus was his state, may Allah be pleased with him: there befell him the calamities of kindness toward his relatives, to which his upright nature led him, until there befell him the great calamities, may Allah be pleased with him. The jim is for 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and it indicates gathering and summation, and the summation that occurs with him is the one most fitting to his affairs, may Allah be pleased with him, for through it gathering occurred after the great division, by the killing of the Commander of the Faithful 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, as a martyr wronged. Summation occurred through him, but detailed clarification was not completed because of the obstinacy that occurred. The ra' is an indication of al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him, and it signifies refinement, transformation, and nurturing, and it belongs to every nurturer, such as a woman's husband and a slave's master. For this reason he acted, may Allah be pleased with him, when he saw the kingdom perishing through the killing of Muslims: he nurtured it by stepping down from the command in favor of Mu'awiyah. He was like a master who grants permission to his slave, and his affair was nurtured by it. The Prophet (ﷺ) had named him "a master" (sayyid). May Allah be pleased with them all, [and Allah knows best what is correct].
